 What a search turns up
 Listings everywhere, answers almost nowhere 
 1 Listings, not answers
 Search for a web designer in Newbury and you get directory listings and social pages, not answers. Your own site may be the same: a page that exists, but does not tell a customer what you do, what it costs or how to book.
 2 A few seconds to decide
 Customers in Newbury and Thatcham decide fast. If your site does not answer their question in the first few seconds, they go back to Google and ring the next name.
 3 A site that answers
 A clear, quick site that answers those questions, shows your areas from Hungerford to Thatcham, and makes it easy to call or ask for a quote.

 How the site gets made
 Questions first, pages second 
 01 List what people ask
 Andy wants to hear what callers ask you week in, week out. That list decides what goes on each page.
 02 Turn it into answers
 He writes those replies in plain words, designs around them and lets you read the whole thing in a preview.
 03 Publish and tell Google
 After your approval, the site moves to your address and goes into Search Console, with enquiries landing straight with you.

 Answers, as promised
 What Newbury firms ask before they ring 
 Thatcham and Hungerford: are they covered as well?
 Yes, along with the rest of West Berkshire, Greenham, Speen, Kingsclere and Lambourn included. Calls and video do most of the work, and your postcode has no effect on the price.
 Can you take over my existing site and domain?
 Yes. Andy builds the replacement as a preview while the old one stays up, then points your domain across at launch once you are happy. The domain stays in your name throughout. You own the site once it is paid for.
 Is a 5-page site enough?
 For most sole traders, yes. A usual set is home, services, about, areas covered and contact, which gives each common question somewhere to live. A firm with several separate services will get more from the 8-page Core.
 What should a Newbury business budget for a website?
 Allow £600 for the 5-page Starter or £995 for the 8-page Core, and £125 for any page past that. Hosting and care then runs at £10 a month, so you can see the whole cost at the outset.
 How soon could the site be answering customers?
 Think 1 to 3 weeks once the deposit is paid. Having your service details and photos ready at the start pulls it towards the shorter end.
 Who holds the keys when it is finished?
 You own the site once it is paid for. Hosting and care is a service you pay for, not a lease on your own website.

## https://newburywebsitedesign.co.uk/about-andy

The person behind the answers
 Andy Norman, building clearer sites for Newbury 
 Field engineer first, service manager later: Andy spent more than three decades in field service and managed print before founding Antek Automation.
 Plenty of that time went on telling customers plainly where things stood. A Newbury firm gets the same treatment now, and so do the people who land on its website.
 What he checks on any website
 Three things come first. Can a stranger tell what the firm does, roughly what it costs and how to book? When any of those is missing, the design can wait until it is fixed.
 Works from Chantry Way, Andover

 When a website is not the whole job
 Some owners later want an AI chatbot on the site or an AI receptionist on the phone. Andy's website and AI services explains what is on offer, and none of it is needed to get a good site live.
